notes: D14: sub-millimetre gaps exist only in raw pointer/preview input. The input layer resolves snapping (§E.10, screen-pixel tolerances) and quantizes once when it builds an integer-mm command. The geometry normalizer never receives a 0.4 mm gap.
GAP-01 is input-adapter data: it is verified when the drawing/snapping layer exists (PH2-T03), not as a PH0-T02 engine test. GAP-02 and GAP-03 are canonical-command cases.

cases.description: Three walls of a 4000 x 3000 rectangle exist. The user closes the loop; the raw pointer end point is 0.4 mm away from the start junction j1. Junction snap closes the loop on j1 and reuses its ID.
arithmetic: Raw end (0.4, 0) is 0.4 mm from j1 (0,0). At zoom 1 CSS px/mm that is 0.4 px, inside the 12 px junction acquire radius (§E.10 priority 1), so the end snaps to exactly j1 and the command uses j1's ID. The start (0, 3000) is exactly j4.
No new junction is created (junctionCount stays 4; a second junction at (0,0) would violate I5).
The loop closes: 1 bounded face. Clear: X 100..3900 = 3800, Y 100..2900 = 2800 -> 10,640,000 mm2.
Centreline signed area 4000 x 3000 = 12,000,000 with corners in screen-clockwise order.

cases.description: Canonical (integer) command that ends 1 mm beside j1 instead of on it: the engine must not 'helpfully' close the loop. The wall (0,3000)->(1,0) is diagonal, so it is rejected.
arithmetic: dx = 1, dy = -3000 -> not axis-aligned -> rejected in L0 (I4). The model is unchanged.
(1,0) is 1 mm from j1, which is not 'closer than 1 mm' (I5), so the engine has no rule that merges it. Closing such gaps is the snapping layer's job (GAP-01).

cases.description: A canonical command that carries a fractional coordinate is invalid and rejected without change. It must never be repaired by treating it as pointer input.
arithmetic: 0.4 is not an integer. Canonical commands carry integer mm only (§E.1, D14), so the command is rejected; the open model stays exactly as it was.
